gen-gf-noto-serif-makasar-satoshi: Lowercase letters swollen like tightly coiled rope give Noto Serif Makasar its literary, slightly rounded-at-the-sides look. And Satoshi supplies the approachable counterweight, a true monoline sans with a soaring x-height and an e that never squeezes shut.
gen-gf-noto-serif-makasar-switzer: Rope-coiled serif curves, then wiry steel. Noto Serif Makasar leans on a gentle, medium-low contrast that feels literary, while Switzer's tubular sans-serif strokes and tall waist line bring a Swiss, approachable bend.
gen-gf-noto-serif-makasar-work-sans: Noto Serif Makasar swells its lowercase like coiled rope, with a faint but real shift from thick to thin strokes. Work Sans just draws outlines in one width, with its mean line set high.
gen-gf-noto-serif-malayalam-archivo: Lowercase that nearly rivals its capitals, with a gentle swelling on the curves, gives Noto Serif Malayalam its dignified authority. Archivo sits below with outward-opening curves and a commanding x-height.
gen-gf-noto-serif-malayalam-fs-asap: Dignified and upright, Noto Serif Malayalam has lowercase that rivals its capitals and a soft thickening on every curve. Asap, a plain sans with a body height close to the capitals, reads smoothly and steadily.
gen-gf-noto-serif-malayalam-fs-epilogue: Noto Serif Malayalam brings authority through lowercase that rivals its capitals, with moderate thick-thin transitions along the curves. But Epilogue hums along in a sans with wire-like monoline strokes, tall bodied and curvy, and a little stubby at the ascender tips.
gen-gf-noto-serif-malayalam-fs-fira-sans: Authoritative from the first line, Noto Serif Malayalam lets its crossbars run a bit finer than its main stems. Fira Sans answers with a larger x-height and round bowls whose walls never swell or taper.
gen-gf-noto-serif-malayalam-fs-public-sa: Noto Serif Malayalam draws its lines like a barely tilted calligraphy nib, with lowercase that rivals the capitals. And Public Sans backs it with a hefty, trustworthy sans body whose broad counters keep paragraphs flowing.
gen-gf-noto-serif-malayalam-fs-supreme: Supreme reads crisp, a heavy-looking strip of plain sans text with letters held open rather than curled shut. And Noto Serif Malayalam sits over it with low-to-medium contrast and lowercase that rivals its capitals.
gen-gf-noto-serif-malayalam-general-sans: General Sans reads like one marker tip traced every line, with an x-height filling the line and smooth bends. Noto Serif Malayalam does dignity best, with thin strokes of real weight.
